title: When Claude’s Lights Flicker, Buyers Need an Exit Door

items.claim: Unite.AI reported elevated errors across Claude.ai, the API, Claude Code, and Cowork.
items.note: The source title names all four affected surfaces; its excerpt describes disruption across nearly the entire Claude product line.

items.claim: Anthropic opened an incident after elevated errors affected requests involving some Claude models.
The disruption reached nearly the company’s entire product line.
The evidence does not establish the root cause, shared dependency, failure topology, customer impact, business interruption, compensation, workload volume, or precise incident timeline.
items.note: These are appropriately framed as limits or absences in the available evidence.

items.claim: Shared-service routing and correlated failure are possible scenarios.
items.note: Explicitly labeled as unverified inference, not observed architecture.

items.claim: Separate coincidental incidents are another possible explanation.
The report provides no independently confirmed customer count, loss estimate, official postmortem, or detailed recovery evidence.
items.note: Consistent with the evidence package and phrased as an evidence limitation.

items.claim: The incident does not prove that Anthropic’s architecture or governance failed.
Product breadth can create concentrated operational risk for buyers.
items.note: Procurement analysis and inference, not asserted as a sourced event fact.

claim_check.reason: The article’s event-specific claims match the available Unite.AI evidence. Unsupported mechanisms, impacts, and governance conclusions are explicitly presented as unknowns, scenarios, or inference. No numerical claims or direct quotations require correction.

seo_title: Claude Outage: Build Your AI Exit Door
seo_summary: Claude’s outage exposes a procurement risk: businesses need tested fallbacks, human-takeover triggers, and portability before AI workflows fail.
